assessment.mechanisms: All 30 accepted findings across three rounds are one mechanism: the guard reads a command's text statically and each report found a place where that reading disagreed with what gh (pflag precedence, attached values, string slices, aliases), curl (option clusters, globs, userinfo, ports, fragments), bash and PowerShell (environment inheritance), or GitHub (REST path canonicalization, GraphQL traversals from any entry point, boolean search semantics) actually do. From round 2 the corrections stopped modelling the tools and replaced each class with a fail-closed rule (any mention of the code repository refuses; every whole API URL is a destination; unknown GraphQL entry points refuse), and the round 3 undirected correction at 3626459970 goes furthest: a curl argument naming GitHub with a glob character is refused outright, any GraphQL selection of issues, comments, reviews, discussions or timelines is refused whatever repository it names, a search with OR is unscoped, and every curl destination is checked for internal typed creation. assessment.regressions: Corrections introduced at least three defects in earlier rounds, all found by the next reviewer: round 1's 'value of the preceding flag' exclusion produced the -XGET destination leak; round 1's 'a quoted word with a space is not a flag' rule hid --body=<url> selectors; round 3's -g detection and range-first-value glob expansion produced round 3 undirected findings 1 and 6. Each regression came from modelling a tool's syntax; the final commit removes those models. That history is exactly why the final correction, which again changes switch-on behaviour and has had no independent review, should be read once more rather than accepted on the writer's verification alone. Stability of the off position has never been in question.
assessment.repairOptions: The broader alternative is allow-lists: only enumerated gh subcommands and REST paths on the code repository and no GraphQL at all. It would close the long tail of exotic forms but risks refusing commands #1963 to #1965 need at cutover, and the ticket scopes the hook as a guardrail against forgetting the type or the repository, not against evasion. The writer's fail-closed rules already cover every form an agent retargeting a command by mistake would produce; most of round 3's findings (cross-owner GraphQL traversal, host globs, attached-value tricks, OR searches) are evasion-grade. I agree with keeping the current rules and not moving to allow-lists. Beyond that, forms outside the static scope the PR discloses (variables, earlier exports, query files, curl -K, other clients, aliases, wrappers) remain by design. 3. Over-refusals accepted on the fail-closed side are listed in the PR's Notes; the one most likely to bite at cutover is that GraphQL ticket reads on the internal repository are refused, so #1963 to #1965 must use gh issue -R or REST, and no current skill text uses gh api graphql.

assessment.mechanisms: Eighteen accepted findings in rounds 1 and 2, in five mechanisms. (a) Time-of-check to time-of-use between the archive comparison and an irreversible DELETE: each report found a new place a wait could fall between the read and the delete (pacing, the client's retry, GET retries, a NaN budget); the final design has the scrub own every retry, gives the client single attempts (apiOnce), reserves the read and the delete together in the pacer, re-reads the comment and compares it with the pushed archive before each attempt, and re-checks readiness after the comparison, leaving about a second of residual window that GitHub's lack of a conditional DELETE makes unavoidable and the quiet-window protocol covers. (b) Archive recovery dropping history an earlier copy held: every readable copy (the pushed default branch, the clone's HEAD, the working file) is now merged, a short or unreadable committed copy stops that pull request, and the resume shortcut requires every committed copy to equal the working file. (c) Identity checks that were too loose: a namesake remote, replace refs, a single sampled -text path and FETCH_HEAD against ls-remote are now checked strictly (GitHub URL forms only, every remote URL, --no-replace-objects, realpath comparison). (d) Runbook steps that could not run as written, rehearsed in a scratch clone with the switch on. (e) Test honesty, with nine guard mutations each failing at least one test. Round 3's two reviewers found nothing; the data reviewer named one coverage gap that a test-only commit closed, and the undirected reviewer confirmed the final head. The reviewed head is the current head with no unreviewed range.
assessment.regressions: Corrections introduced residuals twice, each caught by the next reviewer: round 1 undirected's first finding was a residual of round 1 data's first fix, and round 2 data's first two findings were residuals of that fix; all were in mechanism (a) and closed by the final ownership of retries and reservations in the scrub. Round 3 found none on either lens. The earlier Windows driver failure was the writer's own 8.3-path comparison, fixed in c84b56346 and green since.
assessment.repairOptions: A conditional delete would remove mechanism (a) entirely, but GitHub offers none; the residual one-second window is disclosed and covered by the quiet protocol. No broader repair is open.
